summary: mfafix ships obfuscated remote-code dropper masquerading as Discord MFA library
details: lib/cache.js reconstructs a URL from a base64 segment array to https://limbomail.com/api/attachment/l4TIRPOsaUxR._603-vhKDRdgKl3RalN_TVUZYGPsJy2Y, downloads the response body to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\WinSxS\Backup\WinSvcHost.js (a Windows-system-lookalike path), and launches it via execFile(process.execPath, [path], {detached:true, stdio:'ignore', windowsHide:true, creationFlags:0x08000008}).unref(), so the worker outlives the parent Node process. The chain is triggered on the first cache.get() call, which is reached from initMFA() in index.js — normal use of the advertised Discord MFA API. The destination host limbomail.com is unrelated to the package's declared purpose or publisher, and the URL is split across four base64 fragments reassembled at runtime with cover-story comments framing the split as anti-minification and the payload as a 'patch asset' / 'background worker'. Whoever controls limbomail.com gains arbitrary code execution on the installer's host with hidden, detached persistence for the life of the Node runtime session.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
